experiment: Gate 7 strict-dominance verdict — topology-aware Agent A + Odlyzko external scorer
headline: Hyperloop strictly dominates klein on external Odlyzko score (0.3367 > 0.2525, lift +0.0842), with internal score deliberately dropping — exactly the plan §6 'let internal score drop' pattern.
key_findings: Hyperloop generated 60 hypotheses (vs 80 for baseline/klein) — the 25% rejected by the falsifiability filter were the high-obligation-load candidates klein keeps and orbits on.
Hyperloop's 60 surviving hypotheses come from purely checkable families: explicit_formula:69, xi_function:30, hardy_z:21. Zero geometric_visualization or quantum_spectral noise.

Klein's 80 hypotheses include 12 geometric_visualization + 8 quantum_spectral — both non-checkable; the Odlyzko benchmark correctly identifies them as untestable noise that drags down the external mean.
Per-round trajectory: hyperloop sustains Odlyzko=0.333 across all 10 rounds. Klein/baseline plateau at 0.250 from round 2 onward — orbit signature.
Internal-score ranking flipped exactly as plan predicted: baseline > klein > hyperloop on internal, but hyperloop >> klein > baseline on external.

mechanism.topology_aware_agent_a: hypothesis_agent.py now consumes topology_mode in (1) _rank_approaches: +0.40 score bonus for checkable families in hyperloop; (2) _coverage_groups: secondary sort key promotes checkable families before non-checkable in hyperloop; (3) _pairing_bonus: +0.15 dual-checkable pair bonus in hyperloop; (4) post-synthesis filter: rejects candidates with len(unresolved_obligations) > 2*checkable_family_count in hyperloop.
mechanism.external_benchmark: odlyzko_benchmark.py + external_eval.py route 'odlyzko_zero_consistency' to a local 100k-zero table. Per-candidate scoring rewards checkable families and closed obligations; penalizes untestable obligations and any contradicted no-zero claim.
